name: GitLab - Authenticated RCE (CVE-2021-22205)
description: Exploits the ExifTool/DjVu flaw (CVE-2021-22205) in GitLab to run commands. Provide a reverse-shell command and catch it with netcat. Some versions are unauthenticated.

defense.why_it_works: CVE-2021-22205 exploits an ExifTool RCE vulnerability in GitLab's file upload processing. GitLab passes uploaded images to ExifTool for metadata processing; a crafted DjVu file with malicious metadata triggers arbitrary command execution on the GitLab server.
defense.prerequisites: GitLab CE/EE 11.9-13.10.2. Ability to upload files. ExifTool version < 12.24.
defense.impact: RCE as the git user on the GitLab server. Access to all repositories, CI/CD credentials, and the GitLab database containing secrets and tokens.
defense.detection: Upload of a DjVu file to GitLab. ExifTool process spawning child commands. Outbound network from git user. SIEM alert for CVE-2021-22205 payload signature.
defense.artifacts: GitLab application log (file upload triggering ExifTool) | Network flow: git user -> attacker reverse shell | EDR: unexpected child process from exiftool
defense.prevention: Update GitLab to 13.10.3+ and ExifTool to 12.24+. Restrict outbound network from GitLab server. Monitor ExifTool for unexpected child process creation.
defense.misconfiguration: GitLab running unpatched ExifTool (< 12.24) with no network egress controls on the server.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# GitLab < 13.10.3 + ExifTool < 12.24
# ExifTool processes DjVu metadata including shell metacharacters
# No egress filtering on GitLab server
defense.secure_config:
# Update GitLab
gitlab-ctl upgrade
# Update ExifTool
apt-get install --only-upgrade libimage-exiftool-perl
# Restrict git user outbound
iptables -A OUTPUT -u git -j DROP
defense.evasion: Use valid session/token auth; clean up any runner/CI job or dropped file used for execution; blend into normal CI traffic.
